comparisons.peer_topic: Time deposits accounted for at fair value
comparisons.peer_summary: Time deposits included $44.86 billion as of December 2024 and $29.46 billion as of December 2023 accounted for at fair value under the fair value option.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs discloses time deposits accounted for under the fair value option, specifically noting amounts for both the current and prior fiscal years (Dec 2024 and Dec 2023). Similarly, Bank of America discloses consumer and commercial loans accounted for under the fair value option, also referencing the current and prior fiscal years. Both disclosures quantify the specific balance sheet items elected into the fair value option for the comparable reporting periods, whereas the target explicitly breaks down loan types (mortgage, home equity, commercial).

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value option election for lending-related commitments
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the contractual amount of lending-related commitments for which the fair value option was elected was $12.2 billion and $9.7 billion, respectively, with corresponding fair values of $50 million and $97 million.
comparisons.comparison: JPMorgan discloses the contractual amounts of lending-related commitments for which the fair value option was elected for both December 31, 2024, and December 31, 2023. This is directly comparable to Bank of America's disclosure of consumer and commercial loans accounted for under the fair value option for the same two periods. Both firms utilize the fair value option for specific lending instruments and report the associated volumes for the current and prior fiscal year ends.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment of loans at fair value
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans for which the fair value option is elected are carried at fair value within Trading assets, with changes recognized in earnings. This accounting treatment excludes these loans from the allowance for credit losses and charge-off policies.
comparisons.comparison: Morgan Stanley provides the specific accounting treatment for loans where the fair value option is elected, stating they are carried at fair value within Trading assets with changes recognized in earnings. This supports the context of Bank of America's disclosure, which lists the specific fair value option loan balances (consumer and commercial). While BAC provides the quantitative amounts for these elections, MS explains the mechanics of the election (exclusion from allowance for credit losses) and classification.

sentences.text: (3)Consumer loans accounted for under the fair value option includes residential mortgage loans of $66 million and home equity loans of $177 million.
Commercial loans accounted for under the fair value option includes U.S. commercial loans of $2.2 billion and non-U.S. commercial loans of $1.2 billion.
Loans for which the fair value option is elected are carried at fair value and included in Trading assets in the balance sheet, with changes in fair value recognized in earnings.
Because such loans and lending commitments are reported at fair value, the allowance for credit losses and charge-off policies do not apply to these loans.
